earliest_provable_divergences.reason: The generated reset slice preserves the measured 20557-cycle execution delta, but the runtime SA-1 CpuContext begins at cycle zero and later accounts only CpuContext.cycles. The pre-execution reset hold is therefore absent from the domain cursor.

The first instruction after the measured reset slice uses base 65C816 timing because the SA-1 timing table has no post-reset entry. This is the first instruction-local duration divergence after normalizing away the reset hold.

accumulated_checkpoint_divergence.reason: Missing post-reset SA-1 memory/arbitration waits accumulate across the second block move. The runtime has produced the shared-I-RAM release state and reached the poll while the reference is still executing 00:8C2C.

final_upload_loop_audit.conclusion: The final pair is internally consistent with the reference instruction deltas. Its one-byte frame-boundary lag cannot be repaired honestly by shortening a D655 or D658 access.

causal_chain: The SA-1 reset-release origin omits 1454 pre-execution cycles.
Post-reset SA-1 access waits first diverge at 00:8C23 and accumulate through 00:8C2C.
The runtime reaches 00:8C58 73312 master clocks before the reference identity timestamp.
The staged probe exposes shared-I-RAM completion and releases the waiting S-CPU from this early checkpoint.
The otherwise-correct upload loop therefore arrives at first endFrame with a different instruction phase.

claims.required_correction_scope: Model the SA-1 reset-release timestamp and post-reset access/arbitration waits in a genuinely interleaved scheduler before claiming exact S-CPU frame phase.
